title: I was pleased to participate in a panel discussion today with Minister Jack Chambers, Peter Mullan An Coimisiún Pleanála and Karen C., Maritime Area Regulatory Authority to discuss Regulatory Reform… | Eimear Cotter
description:
I was pleased to participate in a panel discussion today with Minister Jack Chambers, Peter Mullan An Coimisiún Pleanála and Karen C., Maritime Area Regulatory Authority to discuss Regulatory Reform – Progress and Impacts. My key messages were:

The EPA prioritises infrastructure delivery as part of our regulatory functions and the work of the Accelerating Infrastructure Taskforce has certainly sharpened our focus. 

Our priority is to support delivery of critical national infrastructure, while upholding the environmental standards that the public expects and legislation demands.

We have made real and concrete changes in how we organise our people, how we manage work and how we engage with those bringing forward essential projects. We now have more people working on wastewater and water abstraction licensing and have established a new process design team.

We are publishing monthly licensing performance data to enhance transparency and accountability. We are proactively engaging with stakeholders and licensees to communicate our requirements and hear where improvements are needed.

Looking ahead, legislative reform is essential. Recent amendments to the EPA Act for industrial licensing - including the introduction of statutory timelines and partial licence reviews - are welcome.  

Acceleration doesn’t mean cutting corners. We support the delivery of infrastructure while maintaining the safeguards that protect peoples’ health, our environment and builds public trust. 

We are committed to making practical, targeted changes that support the State’s priorities while maintaining legally robust and sound decisions that protect the environment.

title: Emergency Petition Urges EPA to Add Cancer Warnings to Pesticide Labels
description:
The Center for Biological Diversity petitioned the Environmental Protection Agency today to add cancer warnings to all pesticide product labels containing ingredients the agency has linked to cancer.

The emergency filing comes just days after the Supreme Court sided with Bayer and the Trump administration in limiting Americans’ ability to sue pesticide companies for harms, like cancer, linked to many pesticides.

The EPA has routinely failed to put cancer warnings on pesticide products even when its own assessments have found a high risk of those products causing cancer, according to an analysis released earlier this year by the Center.
